I learned to mask my ADHD then and kept it masked until the last 10 years as I got older and had more health issues that were disrupting my executive functioning. I wanted to not only be a voice for women with ADHD but also for living with multiple autoimmune disorders. But transparency doesn’t mean people are going to understand you any better. Only the people who love through what you do will understand. And as we get older our ADHD can get worse and with one of my diagnosis’s being in the same executive function area as my ADHD it makes being ADHD even harder now. title: Innovative in a Simple
body:
At first glance this looks overly simple... Especially when you compare it to all those amazing task apps out there (and I've tried every one of them.)

But I'm discovering that I may have ADHD and I have a history of setting up complex systems and discarding them ... From one app to another.

Part of it is that other apps don't really fit how I work or think. This does.

It's one list with easy capture that can be sorted quickly. It can be reorganized by you or AI. That's all I need to focus on what needs done.

It might be useful to be able to add events from our calendar as tasks, so we have a quick and clear view of our day and we can organize around events.

I also think the prioritization and tagging can be improved, but I like that there is no unnecessary AI stuff.

Most AI tools in task apps have no use for me.

title: Great tool, makes life less overwhelming
body:
I’ve been using the app for about 10 days. It has made tasks & life in general less overwhelming. Obviously, there are similar apps out there, so here are specific things I like about this one:
(sorry for any misspelling 😁) 

1)  COMMUNITY:  I have a hard time on social media apps. I feel like I join them to keep in touch with friends, but I rarely see posts from my own friends on my feed. Instead, I get drowned in random content from accounts I don’t know, which can be nice… but it doesn’t make me feel engaged with MY community. They overwhelm me & give me anxiety. 
But…
Numo allows me to connect with people and give and receive support. You join a team of your own choosing, engage with them as much as you have the capacity, AND there are no random content or interactions from accounts that you never asked for. You don’t end up losing 3 hours of your day on content you never intended to consume.
💕Best part is that I know literally everyone on the app has ADHD & I learn so much about my own brain from others!!! 💕

2)  TASKS: 
         a)  You can choose to make tasks a 1-time thing or a routine. For routines, you can schedule it on specific days & times. 
          b) When creating tasks, you can break them into sub-tasks. And you can complete a general task even if you skipped a sub-task. 

3) 💕STREAKS:  I like that the streak is for the number of days you engage with the app. So, even if you skip a routine, as long as you complete 1 task that day & engage with your team, you don’t lose your streak. 
For me losing a streak is a HUGE discouraging thing. I might just give up on using the app. So, it’s nice that there’s no pressure on completing EVERYTHING just so I don’t lose my streak.

title: Frustrating. Inaccessible. I really tried but i give up.
body:
Good idea in concept, but unusable. I was excited to try the app while looking for ADHD tools, but now i’m just disappointed. 

Half the features are locked, you only have access to the in-app community if you pay (which is ridiculous because ADHDers are in critical need of community for both emotional and functional needs), and you can’t even edit the items in your current day’s tasklist once you’ve posted them — only routine/repeating tasks, or tasks for future dates, can be edited. If you mess up anything in the task or just need to adjust it later, have fun erasing it and creating a whole new task — you better hope it wasn’t the one with like 10 sub-steps because you’re gonna hate it real quick.

(Oh, and minor bug of little importance — the app icon never changes, no matter which customization option i choose. Bummer, because i love Halloween themes and designs, and i was really into the franken-icon.)

Sorry for the negative review. Maybe the developer is still learning (or ADHD has them forgetting to fix things) — i’d like to try using it again in the future, when it works better. But as it is right now, i wouldn’t spend another day on this app if you paid me. Functioning is hard enough as it is.

title: Beautiful app; really appeals to my ADHD troubles and motivates me to use it.
body:
Disclaimer: I was invited to a clinical trial and given 3 months free of the premium subscription, so I don’t know what the free version of the app is like. 

Pros: 

The app design is top-tier for (my) ADHD. The interface is minimalistic, colorful, and simple to use. It has satisfying sounds and haptics, but not so much as to be annoying. It has a reward system for using the app and its features. The rewards only unlock aesthetics (themes, icons, etc.). It has a community feature which I have yet to use. 

Cons: 

The app has some minor typos. It has learning courses that are concise. It has a reader function for the text and some memes to go along with it. The app allows you to customize the speed of the reader and also the time delay after the slide is finished. HOWEVER, my experience with the customization was disappointing. I don’t like to hear a voice while reading text. I’d rather just read the text without the voice; or, listen to the voice while associated images are displayed. The problem I’ve noticed: I can turn off the voice but the slides automatically move on and I can’t read fast enough or process the information before it advances. This, of course, depends on your reading speed. For me, this is a MAJOR block to using the app effectively, and I would love to have an option to advance slides MANUALLY. 

Overall, I’d gladly give it 5 stars and will update my review if this ever gets changed. The app is wonderful to look at and use! Thank you for inviting me to the clinical trial, I’m looking forward to improving my ADHD symptoms using it.

title: Solid proof of concept, priced as if highly polished
body:
This app is on to something amazing, and I wish I could stay subscribed. I love the social media story-style lessons, the community aspect is excellent, and the way the to-do list can break down and prioritize is so helpful!

However, there is a lack of polish that makes it hard to justify the current cost ($59.99 for only six months). Here are the things I noticed that are keeping me from subscribing.

1) Repeating tasks. The limited options work out fine for me, but these tasks will disappear from your list if left incomplete (except for daily). While a regular task will show that it’s overdue, repeating tasks won't. If I have a weekly or monthly task, I need it to stay until I complete it, not limit it to just that one day.

2) Tools introduced in lessons aren't always accessible. Specifically, I love the “find an absurdly small first step to touch your task” hack, but a way to trigger that guidance with any task would be so helpful! I'm sure that's not the only one.

3) Reliance on AI. To be clear, I love the AI features! Super helpful when you cannot make decisions yourself. However, if I want to do the manual prioritization, I must wait for the AI to load first. Sometimes it won't load, so I can't access the manual option that I often prefer. Similarly, I cannot manually add task breakdowns after the AI split. It's either accept or deny the suggested splits only.

I enjoyed my 5 weeks using this app, but I can't justify the cost given the polish it needs to be worth it. I'm sad that I won't have Numo to use day by day, but I know that it's too much of a financial commitment for me. Numo, I hope you consider some of these changes and polishes that your app deserves because this will help so many ADHDers.

title: Tried so many apps - this one is by far the best
body:
I have ADHD and struggle constantly with task management. I’ve tried lots of methods and apps, and nothing has really worked for me so far. A lot of the apps, even if they were fun at first, got to be a task in and of themselves, and the rewards for using the app were low. Most of them are basically glorified to-do lists.

This app is stimulating to look at, uses game-like wording and structure, has lots of mini-courses to help manage different parts of your life (with audio, text, and images that play through automatically - I didn’t zone out at all, which is saying something), forces you to set rewards for yourself for certain tasks, and uses peer support, which is super helpful.

While some of the information isn’t particularly new to me (I’ve read a lot about procrastination, for example), it’s phrased in this straightforward, no-nonsense way that still acknowledges the difficulty of some of these tasks, and it’s addressed specifically to ADHD problems, rather than just general organization issues. It’s incredibly refreshing.

Overall, it really feels like this app was designed specifically for people with ADHD, as opposed to other apps, which feel like basic productivity helpers marketed toward ADHD-ers to take advantage of the demographic. If you have ADHD, really can’t recommend it enough.

title: It’s a cool idea but needs work. Right now it is not worth the price tag.
body:
This is a pretty cool app which allows you to read other peoples tips and tricks for dealing with their ADHD as well as post things you might need help with and get feedback. The problem is that it’s very hard to find your post after you’ve published it and there doesn’t seem to be a way to easily view peoples comments on it without endlessly scrolling to find your post again. 

The to do list feature, prioritization, and prompts to break down your task into the smallest bits to help you get started were all super helpful for me, but I can easily do all of that myself with a pen and paper for free. 

The stories they provide contain information on motivation, procrastination, emotional regulation, etc.. They break concepts down into easily understandable bits. 
However, I personally knew all of the tactics provided just from reading, watching ADHD Youtubers, and viewing content on other platforms. 
It’s great to have these resources in one place, I cannot deny that. But I don’t think it is enough to justify a $16 a month subscription.

You can see other peoples posts and respond to them but there is no way to message anyone directly (which I understand) or to add someone as a friend (which I don’t understand).
Your “squad” is assigned to you (unless you invite your IRL friends and they download the app to join you). There’s no messaging feature in the “squad” either or a way to encourage others besides just liking their posts and to do lists. It doesn’t feel like there is a real way to build community and support networks on this app, which was part of the marketing and what I was looking for.   

I think the concept of this app is awesome. And I would gladly come back to it in the future if it had more to offer. 

The team behind the app is easy to contact and they respond rather quickly. 

I have a lot of hope for the future of Numo! And I can’t wait to check back later to see what was added, but right now it’s just not worth the cost for me.

Yeah we’ve done the numbers and it’s gonna be lucrative to profit off of ppl’s disabilities while rationalizing “it’s because we offer support.” Nope, you’re just greedy capitalists capitalizing on an idea to “provide help” whilst providing you a lifestyle and income. You’re just money addicts. Disgusting.

title: It’s Not a Free Trial
body: I shouldn’t have to accept payment formalities for a “free” trial let alone give my information… for something I am unable to even get a glimpse of before making a decision on whether I want to utilize it or not.
author: sndiskcofm

title: Not worth it
body:
Advice is basic and I feel talked down to. We’ve been coping for ADHD for a long time, I need advanced tactics. 

How can I trust a company to give me advice about ADHD when they charge you automatically when the free trial is over? It seems like taking advantage of us because we are more likely to forget to cancel. It’s about conforming to capitalist demands rather than caring for people with ADHD.
author: Claire B. H.

title: good but needs improvements
body: there are many things that this app does well, but there are two main issues that would prevent me from subscribing. first, this app does not seem to be written well in english. i am not sure if it’s translated to english, but either way it needs to be written better. it’s written well enough that i know what it’s saying, but it takes a lot of mental energy to understand. secondly, $15-$16 a month is waaaaaaaay too expensive for this app. especially considering this app is for people with ADHD, it should be priced at $1-$3/month. with those improvements, i would definitely subscribe and continue using this app. and before i get a reply from one of the app developers saying “oh but a subscription to this app is ____ less than an ADHD coach on average,” why do you think so many of us don’t seek out ADHD coaches? when you price the app so highly it makes me feel as though the app is trying to profit from my disability rather than help. if these changes are made i will happily edit my review to 5 stars, because otherwise i think the app has some very useful features. also, just wanted to add that it’s very obvious that lots of the reviews are fake, which feels dishonest especially when creating an app to help individuals with ADHD.
